# core/aesmodes.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/aesmodes.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

AES in counter, CBC, ECB and XTS mode (NIST SP 800-38A),
on the block cipher of core/aes.bastio.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the result is
as long as the input. Not proved: that the output is the standard's (the
tests check the vectors of SP 800-38A F.2 and F.5), or that the code is
constant time (see core/aes.bastio). CBC and ECB take whole blocks only (ECB leaks equal blocks: use it only to build other modes); padding is
the caller's, and so is the integrity check: neither mode authenticates.

`import "core/aesmodes.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/aes.bastio](core-aes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`aes_ctr`](#aes_ctr) | `data` xor the AES-CTR keystream that starts at the 16-byte counter block `iv`; the whole block counts up as one big-endian number, wrapping at 2^128 (the counter of Linux's `ctr(aes)`). |
| [`aes_cbc_encrypt`](#aes_cbc_encrypt) | CBC encryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks, under the 16-byte `iv`. |
| [`aes_cbc_decrypt`](#aes_cbc_decrypt) | CBC decryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks, under the 16-byte `iv`. |
| [`aes_ecb_encrypt`](#aes_ecb_encrypt) | ECB encryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks. |
| [`aes_ecb_decrypt`](#aes_ecb_decrypt) | ECB decryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks. |
| [`aes_xts_encrypt`](#aes_xts_encrypt) | XTS encryption (IEEE 1619, the disk mode of Linux's `xts(aes)`) of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks, under the data key `k1`, the tweak key `k2` and the 16-byte `tweak` (the sector number, little endian). |
| [`aes_xts_decrypt`](#aes_xts_decrypt) | XTS decryption of `data`; the arguments are those of `aes_xts_encrypt`. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `aes_ctr`

```bastio
fn aes_ctr(a: &Aes, iv: &Bytes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(iv) == 16 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

`data` xor the AES-CTR keystream that starts at the 16-byte counter block
`iv`; the whole block counts up as one big-endian number, wrapping at 2^128
(the counter of Linux's `ctr(aes)`). Encrypts and decrypts alike.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let iv = balloc(16);
let mut data = balloc(20);
let mut i = 0;
while i < 16 {
  bset(&mut key, i, cast[u8](i));
  i = i + 1;
}
let a = aes128_new(key);
let sealed = aes_ctr(a, iv, data);
let back = aes_ctr(a, iv, sealed);
let ok = bytes_eq(back, data) && blen(sealed) == 20;
bfree(back);
bfree(sealed);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(iv);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `aes_cbc_encrypt`

```bastio
fn aes_cbc_encrypt(a: &Aes, iv: &Bytes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(iv) == 16 && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

CBC encryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks, under the
16-byte `iv`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let iv = balloc(16);
let data = balloc(32);
let a = aes128_new(key);
let sealed = aes_cbc_encrypt(a, iv, data);
let back = aes_cbc_decrypt(a, iv, sealed);
let ok = bytes_eq(back, data) && blen(sealed) == 32;
bfree(back);
bfree(sealed);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(iv);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `aes_cbc_decrypt`

```bastio
fn aes_cbc_decrypt(a: &Aes, iv: &Bytes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(iv) == 16 && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

CBC decryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks, under the
16-byte `iv`.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(32);
let iv = balloc(16);
let data = balloc(16);
let a = aes256_new(key);
let back = aes_cbc_decrypt(a, iv, data);
let again = aes_cbc_encrypt(a, iv, back);
let ok = bytes_eq(again, data);
bfree(again);
bfree(back);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(iv);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `aes_ecb_encrypt`

```bastio
fn aes_ecb_encrypt(a: &Aes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

ECB encryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks: each block
on its own, so equal blocks give equal ciphertext. Use it only where a
protocol or interface asks for it.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let data = balloc(32);
let a = aes128_new(key);
let sealed = aes_ecb_encrypt(a, data);
let back = aes_ecb_decrypt(a, sealed);
let ok = bytes_eq(back, data) && blen(sealed) == 32;
bfree(back);
bfree(sealed);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

```bastio
fn aes_ecb_decrypt(a: &Aes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

ECB decryption of `data`, a whole number of 16-byte blocks.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let data = balloc(16);
let a = aes128_new(key);
let sealed = aes_ecb_encrypt(a, data);
let back = aes_ecb_decrypt(a, sealed);
let ok = bytes_eq(back, data);
bfree(back);
bfree(sealed);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `aes_xts_encrypt`

```bastio
fn aes_xts_encrypt(k1: &Aes, k2: &Aes, tweak: &Bytes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(k1) && aes_ok(k2) && blen(tweak) == 16 && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

XTS encryption (IEEE 1619, the disk mode of Linux's `xts(aes)`) of `data`,
a whole number of 16-byte blocks, under the data key `k1`, the tweak key
`k2` and the 16-byte `tweak` (the sector number, little endian). Ciphertext
stealing for a last partial block is not done. Like ECB it does not
authenticate.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let mut key2 = balloc(16);
let tweak = balloc(16);
let data = balloc(32);
let a = aes128_new(key);
let b = aes128_new(key2);
let sealed = aes_xts_encrypt(a, b, tweak, data);
let back = aes_xts_decrypt(a, b, tweak, sealed);
let ok = bytes_eq(back, data) && blen(sealed) == 32;
bfree(back);
bfree(sealed);
aes_free(b);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(tweak);
bfree(key2);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `aes_xts_decrypt`

```bastio
fn aes_xts_decrypt(k1: &Aes, k2: &Aes, tweak: &Bytes, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(k1) && aes_ok(k2) && blen(tweak) == 16 && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

XTS decryption of `data`; the arguments are those of `aes_xts_encrypt`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let mut key2 = balloc(16);
let tweak = balloc(16);
let data = balloc(16);
let a = aes128_new(key);
let b = aes128_new(key2);
let sealed = aes_xts_encrypt(a, b, tweak, data);
let back = aes_xts_decrypt(a, b, tweak, sealed);
let ok = bytes_eq(back, data);
bfree(back);
bfree(sealed);
aes_free(b);
aes_free(a);
bfree(data);
bfree(tweak);
bfree(key2);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `aes_xor16`

```bastio
fn aes_xor16(x: &Bytes, y: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(x) == 16 && at + 16 <= blen(y)
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the 16 bytes of `x` xor the 16 bytes of `y` from `at`.

### `aes_cbc_unchain`

```bastio
fn aes_cbc_unchain(d: &Bytes, iv: &Bytes, data: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(d) == 16 && blen(iv) == 16 && at + 16 <= blen(data) && at % 16 == 0
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: block `at / 16` of the plaintext: `d` xor `iv` for the first,
else xor the ciphertext block before.

### `aes_xts_double`

```bastio
fn aes_xts_double(t: &mut Bytes)
  requires blen(t) == 16
  ensures blen(t) == 16
```

Internal: `t` times x in GF(2^128) with the XTS polynomial, the tweak of
the next block (IEEE 1619): a left shift of the little-endian number,
with 0x87 folded into the low byte when a bit falls off the top.

### `aes_xts_run`

```bastio
fn aes_xts_run(k1: &Aes, k2: &Aes, tweak: &Bytes, data: &Bytes, enc: bool) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(k1) && aes_ok(k2) && blen(tweak) == 16 && blen(data) % 16 == 0 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

Internal: the XTS loop, encrypting or decrypting (`enc`) block by block.

### `aes_xts_core`

```bastio
fn aes_xts_core(k1: &Aes, inv: &Bytes, x: &Bytes, enc: bool) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(k1) && blen(inv) == 256 && blen(x) == 16
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: one block through the first key, either way.
